title: Kenya Confirms Four More Ebola Cases, Total Rises to Seven
excerpt: Three health workers who treated the index patient are among the new Bundibugyo cases, but all four were already in quarantine and 128 of 130 contacts are traced.
body:
• Kenya confirmed four new Ebola Bundibugyo cases on Saturday, including three health workers who treated the country's first patient, taking the total to seven.
  • All four new patients were already in quarantine when they developed fever and tested positive, and the health ministry says there is no evidence of community transmission.
  • Authorities have traced and quarantined 128 of 130 listed contacts, 98.5%, above the 85% benchmark the ministry cites for breaking transmission.
  • There are no approved vaccines or treatments for the Bundibugyo strain; care is supportive.

Kenya confirmed four new cases of the Ebola Bundibugyo virus on Saturday, including three health workers who treated the country's first patient, bringing the total number of confirmed cases to seven, the health ministry said, according to Reuters.

The fourth new case is a male relative of the index patient, who died. The relative had been in quarantine since October 6. Director-General for Health Dr Patrick Amoth said all four developed fever as their first symptom before being isolated and tested, Nairobi News reported. Tests were confirmed at both the National Virology Reference Laboratory and the Kenya Medical Research Institute.

First Transmission Inside Kenya

The cases are the first known infections passed on inside Kenya. The first patient arrived from Congo on October 3, having been ill for about a month; he travelled by road to Uganda and flew to Nairobi, and died on October 5. The three health workers, two men and a woman aged 29, 35 and 32, managed his care on October 3 and 4 and had been in quarantine since October 9.

The second and third patients, confirmed earlier, are stable and responding well to supportive treatment, the ministry said.

Containment Numbers

The ministry said 128 of 130 listed contacts, or 98.5%, had been traced and placed in quarantine, above the 85% global benchmark it cited as needed to break the chain of transmission. Because every new case was already quarantined before symptoms appeared, officials say there is no evidence the virus is spreading in the community, and they assess the risk to the general public as low.

The Congo Link

Kenya's cases are linked to the Ebola epidemic in Congo, the second-largest outbreak ever recorded, with more than 9,000 cases and more than 4,000 deaths. The index patient's journey has raised questions about screening at the Congo-Uganda border, closed since May, and at Nairobi's Jomo Kenyatta International Airport.

Treatment and Monitoring

The new patients are receiving supportive treatment at a designated facility, with their condition closely monitored, the ministry said. Kenya's confirmation protocol requires samples to be examined at both national laboratories before a case is announced, a double check the ministry credits for confidence in the count. Officials attribute the early identification of all four new cases to the quarantine arrangements already in place, which caught the infections before the patients could expose family members or the wider public.

What's Next

Two contacts remain untraced. With no approved vaccine or treatment for the Bundibugyo strain, containment rests entirely on the quarantine net holding while the remaining contacts complete their monitoring period.
